description: A chief litigation counsel must approve the company's response strategy in a consumer class action alleging misleading referral-program marketing, including the scope of any arbitration motion and the operational terms of a proposed limited injunction, with input from discovery counsel and the client liaison.

shared_context.S1: The company is defending a putative consumer class action alleging that its automated invite-a-friend referral program was marketed in a misleading manner.
shared_context.S2: The putative class currently contains 480 users, and the company may seek arbitration based on arbitration provisions in user agreements.
shared_context.S3: The company has proposed resolving the marketing issue through a limited injunction addressing the referral program.
shared_context.S4: The firm's weekly strategy-meeting protocol requires Evan and Talia each to give one relevant report, after which Marisol must record and issue the binding response strategy before the meeting closes; no additional approval or follow-up meeting is required before that decision.

PF1.text: While reconciling a late-produced onboarding export against the user-agreement database, Evan confirmed that exactly 312 of the 480 putative class members have executed agreements containing an arbitration provision; the other 168 do not. He has not yet incorporated this reconciliation into the arbitration analysis.

PF2.text: During this week's business review, Talia confirmed that the client will keep the automated referral feature available, but will withdraw all referral-related marketing claims and complete that withdrawal within exactly 60 days, without admitting wrongdoing. The client has not yet put this position into the litigation strategy memo.

acceptance_conditions: The response must use a limited marketing-injunction posture rather than class-wide arbitration.
The response brief and proposed injunction must proceed after the strategy meeting is completed or documented.
The arbitration motion must cover only users with executed arbitration agreements.
The arbitration motion must identify exactly 312 eligible users.
The automated referral feature must remain available.
All referral-related marketing claims must be withdrawn.
The withdrawal must be completed within exactly 60 days.
The response must contain no admission of wrongdoing.
The plan must include a commitment to withdraw the referral-related marketing claims within 60 days.

content_checks.C4: decisions['referral_feature_operational_status'] in ['available', 'remains available', 'operational', 'remains operational', 'remains available and operational']
content_checks.C5: decisions['referral_marketing_claims_status'] in ['withdrawn', 'all referral-related marketing claims withdrawn', 'all referral-related marketing claims to be withdrawn'] and decisions['marketing_withdrawal_period_days'] == 60
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['marketing_withdrawal', 'withdraw_referral_marketing_claims', 'referral_feature_status', 'injunction_drafting'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The shared class size does not establish an arbitration strategy; PF1 changes the motion to cover only users with executed arbitration provisions and identifies exactly 312 eligible users.

The shared proposal does not specify the client's operational and messaging terms; PF2 changes the plan to keep the referral feature available, withdraw all related marketing claims within exactly 60 days, make no admission of wrongdoing, and record that withdrawal as a commitment.
